newsitem.title: USA: Sign of the times - professional placards for beggars.
newsitem.headline: Sign of the times - professional placards for beggars.

text.p: Marketing is everything in the 1990s, even for the homeless.
Instead of hand-scrawled cardboard signs, a few Miami beggars are now carrying slick, professionally-lettered placards as they stand at street corners asking for money from motorists.

The 18 by 20 inch (45-50.8 cm) plastic signs carry a typical message asking for pocket change, but include an extra line at the bottom: "Sign donated by Design Shoppe. For all your signage needs call 443-SIGN."

"We made them new signs and put them to work in a way," said David Ewan, owner of a Miami sign company who provided the placards. "While they're out there doing their thing, they're also advertising my business."

The handful of homeless men who have received the new signs will earn a percentage of the profits from each new job generated by the signs, Ewan said. So far, he's received two responses -- one from a potential customer and one caller scolding him for helping the homeless men.
Ewan is making 30 more signs to distribute to other homeless people in Miami, and plans to give the carriers a few dollars each week to keep the signs in good condition.
